# Centroid-map meaning of the three-row compliance

This note turns the exact simultaneous Schur funding comparison into a statement about the actual section-centroid Jacobian. It also gives an exact conic-gradient identity. Neither identity alone determines the final sign in the different-split case.

## 1. A common affine chart of normal vectors

Retain the strict different-split three-full-row configuration of `candidate 0145a0829278406d`. Orient all raw normals toward the unique noncentral vertex h. There is one central vertex k excluded by all three oriented cuts. Normalize its raw entry to -1 and denote the resulting vectors n_X,n_Y,n_Z. Their actual raw margins are

    c_X=s_X n_X, c_Y=-s_Y n_Y, c_Z=s_Z n_Z,
    s_X,s_Y,s_Z>0.

Since c_X+c_Y+c_Z=0, comparison of the k entries gives

    s_Y=s_X+s_Z,
    n_Y=(s_X n_X+s_Z n_Z)/s_Y.                       (1)

All n_i belong to E=b^perp and lie on one affine line in the common two-dimensional chart

    N={n in E:n_k=-1}.

Choose affine coordinates (t,u) in N so that this line is u=0. Let d,e be its coordinate directions, with d tangent to the line. The functional ell annihilating span(n_X,n_Z) in E is normalized by ell(d)=0, ell(e)=1; on the chart it is the u covector.

## 2. Exact Jacobian and scale identity

For a proper h-oriented tetrahedral cap with raw normal n, let P(n) be its probability, f(n) the density at zero of sum n_j Exp_j, and g(n) its actual section centroid. The coarea/size-bias identity is

    grad P(n)=3 f(n) g(n).

At any one of the stationary sections g(n_i)=b, differentiate this equality in the two fixed chart directions. Since b dot d=b dot e=0,

    H_i=3 f(n_i) J_i,                               (2)

where H_i is the 2-by-2 chart Hessian of P and

    (J_i)_{ab}=d_a dot Dg(n_i)[d_b],  (d_1,d_2)=(d,e).

Thus the paired actual centroid Jacobian J_i is symmetric. Equation (2) uses the derivative of the true section centroid, not a chosen or rounded point.

The degree-zero cap and degree-minus-one density scaling give, in this SAME chart,

    Q_X=-J_X/s_X,    Q_Y=J_Y/s_Y,    Q_Z=-J_Z/s_Z.   (3)

The sign reversal for Y is important: its actual cap is complementary to the h-oriented cap, and its actual raw normal is -s_Y n_Y. The opposite orientation has the same zero-density f and complementary cap Hessian.

Suppose the quotient forms are nondegenerate, with J_X,J_Z positive definite and J_Y of signature (+,-), as in the unresolved branch of the funding theorem. Define

    C_i=ell^T J_i^(-1)ell.

Equations (1)–(3) turn the exact funding comparison into

    C_Y < [s_X C_X+s_Z C_Z]/s_Y.                    (4)

A strict inequality in (4) produces an actual feasible positive second variation of all three full rows, including each threshold correction. Formula (4) is independent of the chosen scale of ell and transforms covariantly under any linear change of the chart coordinates. In coordinates chosen above,

    C_i=(J_i)_{tt}/det J_i=3f(n_i)(H_i)_{tt}/det H_i. (5)

Thus (4) is a strict secant comparison of inverse centroid curvature at three actual stationary sections. It is not asserted to follow from convexity of that quantity between them.

## 3. Differentiating an actual-centroid conic identity

Fix one strict 2+2 split and let F_b(n)=0 be the explicit universal conic from `candidate 5db4787053e18091`, written in its chart normal coordinates. Near an actual section of THIS split, the polynomial/rational identity is

    F_{g(n)}(n)=0.                                  (6)

The coefficient parameter b may be varied in the affine hyperplane sum b=1. Let K be a gradient of F with respect to that parameter, regarded as a four-vector modulo multiples of 1. There are unique coefficients kappa_t,kappa_u and some gamma such that, at the stationary section,

    K-(b dot K)1 = kappa_t d+kappa_u e+gamma n.

This follows because (d,e,n) is a basis of E. Different choices of K modulo 1 yield the same two kappa coefficients. Since every actual centroid satisfies sum g=1 and n dot g(n)=0, differentiation at g=b along a chart direction gives

    sum Dg=0,       n dot Dg=0.

Differentiating (6) therefore yields the exact two-vector identity

    J kappa = - grad_(t,u) F_b(n).                  (7)

No inversion of the centroid map is assumed. At a nondegenerate J, (7) gives a directly computable inverse-Jacobian pairing from the conic and its centroid-parameter derivatives.

Write

    a=J_tt, c=J_tu, b0=J_uu,
    F_t=partial_t F_b, F_u=partial_u F_b,
    E0=-kappa_t F_t-kappa_u F_u=kappa^T J kappa.

Whenever kappa_u!=0, elementary elimination of (7) gives

    det J=[a E0-F_t^2]/kappa_u^2,
    C=ell^T J^(-1)ell
      =kappa_u^2 a/[a E0-F_t^2].                   (8)

These identities retain the actual tangential centroid derivative a; the conic alone does not silently replace it.

For a positive-definite J, E0>0 and (8) gives

    C >= kappa_u^2/E0,

with equality exactly when F_t=0. For an indefinite J with a<0, if E0>0 then

    C <= kappa_u^2/E0.

Both inequalities follow by dividing (8) by a and tracking its sign. They are conditional bounds, not a proof that the required E0 sign or secant comparison always holds.

If the same-split pair lies at t=t_X,t_Y on u=0, the conic restricted to that line has the exact form c0(t-t_X)(t-t_Y). Consequently its two F_t values are opposite and equal in magnitude. This can be substituted directly into (8), but the two tangential centroid derivatives remain actual geometric data.

## 4. Cross-split limitation

Identity (6), hence (7), applies only with the conic of the section's own split. For the third, different-split section, evaluation in the FIRST split's conic is strictly negative by the audited cross-split formula. One must not differentiate that evaluation as if it were zero. Differentiating the appropriate cross-split rational identity instead introduces the derivative of its nonzero right-hand side.

Thus the strict negative cross-split value and the conic chord coefficients are retained without turning them into an unsupported inverse-Jacobian equality. Equations (4), (7), and (8) are the precise bridge available at present; a proof of the final strict secant comparison still requires an additional actual geometric argument.
